subject: Post-demo: Privacy handoffs, breach notify windows, and evidence request
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@medsync.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Privacy handoffs, breach notify windows, and evidence request

Hi Samantha — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call plus proposed next steps focused on the privacy/PII items you raised so we can align with your legal and security teams.

Summary of what we heard from MedSync:
- You need clarity on controller vs processor responsibilities across the ingestion and augmentation flows (patient intake -> enrichment -> storage).
- Subprocessor notification expectations and evidence requirements for an initial pilot (60k events/month).
- Log retention needs (audit logs, request tracing) and whether Redwood can provide off-the-shelf retention tiers and exportable evidence.
- Data residency preference for EU customers (applicable later) but confirm where production data for pilot will live.
- Breach notification timing and level of detail you expect in an initial and follow-up report.

Proposed concrete next steps (my ask + what we'll deliver):
1) Redwood to confirm DPA-role mapping for the three flows above (controller v processor responsibilities) and provide suggested wording for your DPA addendum. Target: draft by Mon 24 Aug.
2) Provide a short evidence pack showing logging controls, sample retention policy, and how we surface request-level traces (redwood-dpa-exec-summary.pdf + logs-retention-matrix.csv). Attached.
3) Confirm subprocessor notify window and escalation path. On the call you mentioned legal prefers a fixed initial window. Redwood proposal below.
4) Align breach-notify timeline: we propose an initial notification "without undue delay" and a practical commitment for an interim update within 72 hours and a detailed post-mortem within 10 business days. Please let us know if MedSync needs a shorter SLA (e.g., 48 hours for interim).
5) We'll also include a short checklist for evidence requests we can support programmatically (API access to audit logs, exports, and a sample template for forensic requests).

Attachment references: redwood-dpa-exec-summary.pdf (high-level mapping + sample contract language), logs-retention-matrix.csv (retention tiers, sample export fields).

Please reply with any items I missed and confirm whether your legal team would prefer 48h or 72h for the interim notice. Once you confirm, we'll produce the DPA wording and the evidence pack.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference — inference for production (www.redwoodinference.com)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@medsync.health>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MedSync Legal <legal@medsync.health>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Privacy handoffs, breach notify windows, and evidence request

Thanks Diego — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Role mapping: For our intake flow MedSync is controller (we collect PII), Redwood will be a processor for enrichment and transient storage. For the long-term archive (we may bring to our own storage), we'd like a clear handoff clause that spells out who is responsible for deletion requests.
- Notification window: Legal is asking if Redwood can do an interim notice within 48 hours for incidents that materially impact patient data confidentiality. A full root-cause/post-mortem can remain at 10 business days.
- Subprocessor notify: we need notification of any new subprocessor engaged to process MedSync data 30 days before onboarding during the pilot; for escalations we want contact details for the person responsible at Redwood (not just a team email).
- Logs/retention: we need to confirm export format for request logs (CSV + JSON line format) and a sample field set.

Please send the DPA wording and the evidence pack. Also can you include the person who would be signatory or escalation owner for breach-notify?

Samantha
VP Product Operations
MedSync Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: Privacy handoffs, breach notify windows, and evidence request

Forwarding Samantha's reply — legal wants 48h interim for material incidents and a 30-day notice for subprocessors during the pilot.

Diego / Neha — proposed internal plan to respond:
1) Draft DPA addendum language that: a) maps controller/processor for intake/enrichment/archive; b) adds a deletion handoff clause; c) commits to 30d subprocessor notice for pilot and provides an escalation contact.
2) Tech ops to export sample logs in both CSV and JSONL and confirm available retention tiers (30/90/365 days). We can attach logs-retention-matrix.csv and a small sample export.
3) Security to confirm our incident communications practice and approve proposed external wording: initial notification without undue delay + interim update within 48h for material incidents + post-mortem within 10 business days.

Neha — can you own the logs sample and retention confirmation? Diego I'll let you own the DPA wording and the escalation contact info. I'll draft a recommended signatory line from Security Ops ("Lina Park, Head of Prod Security") and confirm with Lina.

-Marissa
Director, Solutions & GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@medsync.health>, MedSync Legal <legal@medsync.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Privacy handoffs, breach notify windows, and evidence request

Samantha — thanks for the quick turnaround and the specifics. Per Marissa and Neha's notes above, attached is the evidence pack and our suggested DPA snippets (see redwood-dpa-exec-summary.pdf). Key proposed commitments for the pilot: 

- Roles: MedSync = Controller for intake and archive; Redwood = Processor for enrichment and transient storage; deletion requests will be processed by Redwood when data is in our storage and we will provide a documented handoff for archive-state deletions if MedSync pulls data into your systems.
- Subprocessor notice: Redwood will provide written notice 30 days prior to onboarding any subprocessor that will process MedSync data during the pilot. For emergency replacements (critical security patching, etc.) we will notify within 72 hours and provide risk justification.
- Breach comms: Redwood proposes: initial notification without undue delay; interim status update within 48 hours for incidents materially impacting patient data confidentiality (per your ask); and a final root-cause and mitigation report within 10 business days.
- Logs/retention: we can export request logs in CSV and JSONL. Available retention tiers: 30/90/365 days. See logs-retention-matrix.csv for fields and sample export.
- Escalation/contact: Primary escalation owner for security incidents — Lina Park (Head of Prod Security) <lina.park@redwoodinference.com> and Backup — Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>. We'll include direct phone numbers in the formal DPA draft if you'd like them.

If that aligns, we'll package the DPA addendum draft and a short intake checklist for your legal team to complete (contact, signatory names, required residency restrictions if any). If you prefer to loop another MedSync stakeholder into this thread, happy to add them.

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-exec-summary.pdf (see section 2.1 for suggested language); logs-retention-matrix.csv (sample export format).
